History and power on the ballot in Florida governor’s race TALLAHASSEE, Fla. (WFLA) — Florida voters will be heading to the polls Tuesday to decide who will replace Governor Ron DeSantis when his second term ends next year.
 The big question: will Republicans hold onto the governor's mansion? Or will a Democrat be elected?
On Monday, Republican Congressman Byron Donalds joined Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd, U.S. Senator Ashley Moody, Lt. Governor Jay Collins, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, and Attorney General James Uthmeier in Lakeland, where supporters were urged to turn out and vote on Election Day.
"Election Day is tomorrow, and we are going to win, and I am going to be your next governor, Donalds told the crowd.
 Republicans are counting on strong in-person turn out on Tuesday to help secure victory in the governor's race and wins down the ballot.
"More Democrats are voting this year than they did four years ago; that's very clear, but Republicans are about to show themselves out at the polls tomorrow," Donalds said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Donalds' is running on a promise to continue the conservative leadership of Governor Ron DeSantis, lowering insurance, cutting property taxes, and protecting parental rights.
 While Jolly is hoping Floridians are ready for change.
 But this election is not just about who occupies the governor's office, Tuesday's results in other key races across the state could determine whether Florida ends up unified with Republican leadership, or a divided government.
Turn out is going to be key tomorrow for both parties, but there's also history on the line in this election.
 Donalds could become Florida's first black governor, while Jolly could end nearly three decades of Republican control of the governor's mansion.
